A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SETS research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including the new Appendix F in v4.

before.justification: V3 reports original benchmark experiments, scaling curves, component evaluations, ablations, and repeated-run results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical results and adds Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite experiments, including scaling curves and self-verification/self-correction measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same sampling, iterative self-verification/self-correction, early stopping, and majority-voting procedure. The prompts are unchanged. Newly specified matching and invalid-answer handling do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Trip Planning, Meeting Planning, LiveBench Reasoning, MATH500, AIME 2024–2025, and LiveCodeBench TestOutputPred. Appendix A's dataset descriptions and sample counts are unchanged. Summarization, tool use, and multimodal evaluation remain future directions.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain SELF-REFINE, BoN+Majority Vote, BoN+Self-Eval, and BoN+Self-Verify; the oracle comparison is also retained. Appendix F's comparison with Snell et al. is descriptive, not an added empirical baseline.

E3.justification: V4 adds Flash-Lite with a 24,576-token thinking budget. Section 4.2 changes reported thinking-model sampling maxima from 100 to 50 for BoN+Majority Vote/Self-Eval and from 50 to 25 for SETS/BoN+Self-Verify. Non-thinking ranges and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. These revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 2 extends the existing analysis of self-verification and self-correction capabilities to Flash-Lite across all six benchmarks. The correction-round, temperature, verification-sampling, oracle, task-difficulty, and worked-example analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D.8 reports three repetitions and mean ± standard deviation in both versions. No new seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is introduced. Changed standard-deviation values in Table 4 are result changes.

E6.justification: V4 adds a complete six-benchmark Flash-Lite scaling evaluation and component scores, and revises existing planning curves. Under unchanged reported fixed configurations, Table 4 changes Trip Planning SETS accuracy from 71.9±0.3% to 68.5±3.0% and BoN+Self-Verify from 72.0±0.4% to 60.6±9.7%, changing their mean ranking; token costs also change. This substantially expands and revises the reported evidence, without establishing a methodological performance gain.

T1.justification: The judgment function, majority-voting formulation, and compute-constrained optimization definition in Equations 1–3 are retained. Neither version adds distinct theorems or proofs. Revised experimental parameter ranges do not change the mathematical framework.

C1.justification: The central claims remain training-free combination of parallel and sequential scaling, improved accuracy versus the retained baselines, and applicability across planning, reasoning, mathematics, and coding. The up-to-10.9% improvement claim remains. V4 makes previously stated training-free properties more explicit.

C2.justification: V4 adds an interpretation linking higher temperature to broader reasoning exploration, discusses instruction-following and parsing failures, and explicitly identifies objectively verifiable answers and text-only evaluation as applicability boundaries. It explains that broader generation tasks would require different aggregation. Appendix D.8 removes the previous Trip Planning near-tie interpretation.

D1.justification: V4 specifies exact-match voting, exact-match/rule-based correctness evaluation, error-positive precision/recall/F1 evaluation, and the two-round SELF-REFINE procedure behind Table 2. Appendix D.2 newly documents excluding unparsable None answers from majority voting. These disclosures improve implementation clarity; the existing prompts and output schemas are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix F/Table 5 expand the existing comparison with Snell et al., detailing verification, revision, stopping, answer selection, evaluation breadth, and practicality. V4 also adds Chen et al.'s Universal Self-Consistency as a possible aggregation approach for future extensions.

P1.justification: V4 locally rewrites the abstract, introduction, setup, and conclusion, expands explanations and limitations, and adds Appendix F. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes its displayed model-task panels, with displaced results retained in Appendix D.2. V4 adds the Flash-Lite figure and Table 5, expands Table 2, enlarges Table 4, and compacts appendix prompt layouts. The overall visual design is retained.

improvement.justification: V4 improves reproducibility through explicit evaluation and answer-handling details, clarifies applicability limits and its relationship to prior work, and supplies supporting evidence from another model. These are useful refinements to an already developed paper. The unexplained Table 4 revisions limit confidence in the changed ranking and do not independently establish improved experimental reliability.
